correctness.rationale: The complete Martins source was inspected through the relevant topology sections. Its definition gives a unique family member through every point-hyperplane pair and a smooth connected parameter manifold; Proposition 2.6 gives first-order evaluation isomorphisms; Proposition 2.7 identifies two-sided nodal sets with equators; Section 2.2 gives the projective-hyperplane analogue for one-sided members; Theorems A and B give compact ambient topology and parameter-space topology. These inputs justify transversality, the pair-incidence submersion, properness, connected-base surjectivity, Ehresmann local triviality, nearby-fiber identification, and fixed-member isotopy. No gap was found in the globalization argument.

value.rationale: The theorem turns local infinitesimal projective incidence into a global exact law for every pair, including nonlinear Zoll families that cannot be globally straightened, and yields a reusable configuration-space bundle and isotopy classification.

final_claim: For every unoriented transitive family of closed embedded hypersurfaces in ambient dimension at least three, all distinct pairs meet transversely in the standard codimension-two topology, and the ordered pair-incidence space is a smooth fiber bundle.
